key_insight: This paper argues that AI should be actively aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), so technical progress is evaluated not just by accuracy or scale, but by measurable social and environmental value. It reframes AI development around solving real-world sustainability challenges rather than optimizing models in isolation.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between rapid AI advancement and its uneven contribution to global sustainability goals. It tackles the challenge of redirecting AI research, deployment, and evaluation toward outcomes that support people, planet, and equitable development.
method: Proposes an SDG-oriented framing for AI research and deployment.
Connects AI capabilities to sustainability priorities to guide responsible use and evaluation.
Highlights how AI systems can be mapped to development goals across social, economic, and environmental domains.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical lens for choosing projects, defining success metrics, and communicating societal value. It encourages building models that are not only performant, but also aligned with responsible innovation and long-term global impact.
visual_elements: A hub-and-spoke diagram linking AI applications to the 17 SDGs
A before/after pipeline showing 'performance-only AI' versus 'SDG-aligned AI'
An impact matrix mapping AI use cases to social, environmental, and economic outcomes
Icons representing sustainability themes such as climate, health, education, and equity
paper_title: Realigning AI technology towards the Sustainable Development Goals
paper_authors: Rundong Feng, Ziming Li, Bojie Fu, Huadong Guo, Jianguo Liu
